To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
there has been a convergence in the public police sector of business principles and practices, and that police unions have responded in a variety of ways to these developments.
the convergence of police management into a business‐oriented corporate executive has been successful, but that the revitalization of police unionism has been successful as well.

the convergence of police corporate sectors has occurred, and that this process has been accompanied by a convergence of the public and private policing corporate sectors into one ‘police industry’ that is managed by corporate executives.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the convergence of public and private police management and the impact of police unionization on the transfer of business‐oriented principles to public policing.
the transfer of business‐principled management and the impact on the police union movement.
the extent of convergence between public and private police management and the impact of unionized and de‐unionized policing on this process.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
there has been a convergence, but it is not yet complete.
the convergence of police management and policing unions is a process that is not likely to be resolved by the current generation of police managers and unions.
the transfer of business‐principles has had a significant effect on the public police.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
there is a convergence of the public and private police sectors into a police industry.
the convergence of the private and public policing sectors has not stalled, but is likely to continue to develop.
there has been a convergence in police management, and the transfer of business practices has been successful.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the transfer of business management principles to the public sector has been successful, and that this has been accompanied by the emergence of a unionized and non-unionized police sector.
the transfer of business‐principled management is likely to be a permanent feature of policing, and that the unionization of police is likely to remain an important feature of the policing industry.

the transfer of business practices to the public sector is not simply a matter of the public police adopting private sector management techniques; it is also a matter of the private sector adopting public police management principles.
